name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q01 - Elemental composition of living organisms and earth crust

questiontext.text: It is said that elemental composition of living organisms and that of inanimate objects (like earth's crust) are similar in the sense that all the major elements are present in both. Then what would be the difference between these two groups? Choose a correct answer from among the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
All living organisms and inanimate matter (such as the Earth's crust) contain common chemical elements, including carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, calcium, magnesium, and sodium. However, a quantitative elemental analysis reveals marked differences in the relative abundance of these elements per unit mass.

Evaluation
Living tissues are predominantly constituted of organic macromolecules whose structural backbones are formed by carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. When calculated as a percentage of total mass, the relative abundance of carbon, oxygen, and hydrogen is significantly higher in living organisms than in the Earth's crust. In contrast, the Earth's crust is predominantly composed of silicon and oxygen, while elements such as gold and calcium are not found in higher proportions per unit mass in living systems relative to inanimate matter.

Final Conclusion
The key distinguishing feature is that living organisms have more carbon, oxygen, and hydrogen per unit mass than inanimate objects.

answer.text: Living organisms have more gold in them than inanimate objects.
Living organisms have more water in their body than inanimate objects.
Living organisms have more carbon, oxygen and hydrogen per unit mass than inanimate objects.
Living organisms have more calcium in them than inanimate objects.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q02 - Element not found in living organisms

questiontext.text: Many elements are found in living organisms either free or in the form of compounds. Which of the following is not found in living organisms?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Elemental analysis of plant and animal tissues reveals a range of macro- and micronutrients essential for structural integrity, cellular osmotic balance, and metabolic catalysis.

Evaluation
Magnesium, sodium, and iron are vital physiological elements: sodium maintains membrane potential and fluid volume, magnesium acts as an essential cofactor for enzyme systems utilizing ATP, and iron is a crucial component of oxygen-transport proteins and cytochromes. In contrast, standard elemental analyses of living organisms (such as human tissues) show that silicon is negligible or functionally absent.

Final Conclusion
Silicon is the element among the choices that is not found as a constituent in living organisms (present only in negligible amounts).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q03 - Identification of amino acid among organic molecules

questiontext.text: Aminoacids, have both an amino group and a carboxyl group in their structure. Which one of the following is an amino acid?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
An amino acid is an organic molecule that contains an amino group (\(-\text{NH}_2\)), a carboxyl group (\(-\text{COOH}\)), a hydrogen atom, and a variable side chain (\(\text{R}\)-group) all bonded to the central \(\alpha\)-carbon atom.

Evaluation
Formic acid (\(\text{HCOOH}\)) is a monocarboxylic acid without an amino group. Glycerol is a trihydroxy sugar alcohol (\(\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}_3\)). Glycolic acid (\(\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-COOH}\)) is an \(\alpha\)-hydroxy acid bearing a hydroxyl group rather than an amino moiety. Glycine (\(\text{H}_2\text{N-CH}_2\text{-COOH}\)) possesses both an amino group and a carboxyl group attached to the central carbon (where the \(\text{R}\)-substituent is a hydrogen atom), fulfilling the structural criteria of an \(\alpha\)-amino acid.

Final Conclusion
Glycine is the amino acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q04 - Dipolar ion with simultaneous positive and negative charges

questiontext.text: An aminoacid under certain conditions have both positive and negative charges simultaneously in the same molecule. Such a form of aminoacid is called

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
The amino group (\(-\text{NH}_2\)) and carboxyl group (\(-\text{COOH}\)) of an amino acid are ionizable functional groups that respond reversibly to variations in environmental \(\text{pH}\).

Evaluation
At a specific characteristic \(\text{pH}\) (the isoelectric point), the carboxyl group deprotonates into an anionic carboxylate group (\(-\text{COO}^-\)), while the amino group protonates into a cationic ammonium group (\(-\text{NH}_3^+\)). The molecule therefore contains equal numbers of positive and negative formal charges simultaneously, maintaining net electrical neutrality. Such an internal dipolar ion is designated as a zwitterion.

Final Conclusion
An amino acid possessing both positive and negative charges simultaneously in the same molecule is called the zwitterionic form.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q05 - Six carbon monosaccharide carbohydrate classification

questiontext.text: Sugars are technically called carbohydrates, referring to the fact that their formulae are only multiple of C(H₂O). Hexoses therefore have six carbons, twelve hydrogens and six oxygen atoms. Glucose is a hexose. Choose from among the following another hexose.

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Monosaccharides are classified according to the total number of carbon atoms in their skeleton. A hexose sugar contains six carbon atoms and corresponds to the general molecular formula \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\).

Evaluation
Erythrose is a four-carbon tetrose sugar (\(\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_4\)). Ribose and ribulose are five-carbon pentose sugars (\(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5\)), serving respectively as an aldopentose and a ketopentose. Fructose contains six carbon atoms with the molecular formula \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\) and functions as a ketohexose, which shares the same empirical hexose formula as glucose.

Final Conclusion
Fructose is another hexose sugar.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q06 - Phosphorylated nucleoside biomolecule in acid soluble pool

questiontext.text: When you take cells or tissue pieces and grind them with an acid in a mortar and pestle, all the small biomolecules dissolve in the acid. Proteins, polysaccharides and nucleic acids are insoluble in mineral acid and get precipitated. The acid soluble compounds include aminoacids, nucleosides, small sugars etc. When one adds a phosphate group to a nucleoside, one gets another acid soluble biomolecule called

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
A nucleoside is composed of a nitrogenous base covalently linked to a pentose sugar via an N-glycosidic bond. Esterification of a phosphate group to the sugar moiety of a nucleoside yields a nucleotide.

Evaluation
Nitrogenous bases (such as adenine or guanine) are heterocyclic rings without attached sugars or phosphate groups. When a nitrogenous base binds to a pentose sugar, a nucleoside (e.g., adenosine) is formed. When one or more phosphate groups are esterified to the nucleoside at the 5'-hydroxyl position of the ribose/deoxyribose sugar, the resulting monomer is a nucleotide (e.g., adenylic acid or adenosine monophosphate). In cellular fractionation, these monomeric units remain in the acid-soluble micromolecular fraction.

Final Conclusion
Adding a phosphate group to a nucleoside produces a nucleotide.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q07 - Cellular representation of acid soluble pool

questiontext.text: When we homogenise any tissue in an acid the acid soluble pool represents

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Chemical homogenization of biological tissue with trichloroacetic acid partitions cell constituents based on molecular weight and solubility into an acid-soluble pool (filtrate) and an acid-insoluble pool (retentate).

Evaluation
The acid-soluble pool contains small biomacromolecular precursors and metabolites (micromolecules with molecular weights roughly from \(18\) to \(800\text{ Da}\)) dissolved in the aqueous fluid of the cell, which corresponds broadly to the cytoplasmic matrix. Conversely, the acid-insoluble retentate contains insoluble macromolecules (proteins, nucleic acids, and polysaccharides) as well as disrupted organellar and cell membrane fragments (such as nuclei, mitochondria, and plasma membrane vesicles).

Final Conclusion
The acid-soluble pool represents the cytoplasm.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q08 - Most abundant chemical component in living organisms

questiontext.text: The most abundant component of living organisms is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Living systems are aqueous-based chemical environments composed of inorganic constituents and organic macromolecules including proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, and nucleic acids.

Evaluation
Quantitative cellular analysis shows that water is the predominant molecule in living organisms, comprising approximately \(70\%\) to \(90\%\) of the total cellular mass. By comparison, proteins make up \(10\%\) to \(15\%\), nucleic acids represent \(5\%\) to \(7\%\), carbohydrates account for roughly \(3\%\), and lipids account for \(2\%\) of the total cellular mass.

Final Conclusion
Water is the most abundant component of living organisms.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q09 - Heteropolymeric composition of proteins from monomers

questiontext.text: A homopolymer has only one type of building block called monomer repeated 'n' number of times. A heteropolymer has more than one type of monomer. Proteins are heteropolymers usually made of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
A heteropolymer is a biological macromolecule assembled from non-identical monomeric subunits linked in a specific linear order.

Evaluation
Proteins are unbranched heteropolymeric polypeptide chains formed by amino acid residues connected through covalent peptide linkages. Across all living systems, standard proteins are synthesized during translation using a universal repertoire of 20 distinct standard amino acids, each distinguished by a unique side chain (\(\text{R}\)-group).

Final Conclusion
Proteins are heteropolymers composed of 20 types of monomers.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q10 - Physiological functions and hormone role of proteins

questiontext.text: Proteins perform many physiological functions. For example, some functions as enzymes. Which of the following represents an additional function that some proteins discharge?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Proteins carry out diverse physiological roles in biological systems, including acting as biocatalysts (enzymes), structural elements, carrier/transport molecules, immune defense agents (antibodies), and intercellular signaling messengers (hormones).

Evaluation
Several vital hormones (such as insulin, glucagon, and anterior pituitary hormones) are polypeptide or protein molecules that regulate metabolic processes throughout the body. In contrast, antibiotics are typically secondary metabolic products rather than proteins; melanin (skin pigment) is a polymer derived from the amino acid tyrosine; and floral pigments (such as anthocyanins and carotenoids) are non-protein secondary metabolites including flavonoids and terpenoids.

Final Conclusion
Discharging functions as hormones is an additional physiological role fulfilled by proteins.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q11 - Monomeric unit of glycogen homopolysaccharide

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
A homopolysaccharide is a complex carbohydrate composed entirely of identical monosaccharide repeating units linked through glycosidic bonds.

Evaluation
Glycogen functions as the principal glucose storage polysaccharide in animal and fungal cells. It is a branched polymer composed exclusively of \(\alpha\text{-D-glucose}\) monomers linked linearly by \(\alpha\text{-(1}\rightarrow4\text{)}\) glycosidic bonds, with branch points formed by \(\alpha\text{-(1}\rightarrow6\text{)}\) glycosidic linkages. Because it contains only glucose residues throughout its structure, it is a homopolymer of glucose.

Final Conclusion
Glycogen is a homopolymer made of glucose units.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q12 - Relationship of branches to ends in glycogen

questiontext.text: The number of 'ends' in a glycogen molecule would be

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Glycogen is organized as a branched, tree-like macromolecule. Linear polysaccharide chains terminate at non-reducing ends, while the foundation of the macromolecule originates from a single reducing end bound to glycogenin.

Evaluation
In any branched tree network, an unbranched chain has one non-reducing terminal end (and one reducing end). Each branch point introduces an additional chain that terminates in a non-reducing end. Therefore, if a glycogen molecule has \(n\) branch points (branches), the number of non-reducing terminal ends equals \(n + 1\). Thus, the number of terminal ends in the branched architecture is equal to the number of branches plus one.

Final Conclusion
The number of ends in a glycogen molecule is equal to the number of branches plus one.

answer.text: Equal to the number of branches plus one
Equal to the number of branch points
Two, one on the left side and another on the right side

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q13 - Number of ends in primary protein structure

questiontext.text: The primary structure of a protein molecule has

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
The primary structure of a protein refers to the linear, unbranched chain of amino acids joined together by peptide bonds.

Evaluation
A linear unbranched polypeptide chain has two distinct terminal ends: the N-terminal end (bearing a free \(\alpha\)-amino group on the first amino acid) and the C-terminal end (bearing a free \(\alpha\)-carboxyl group on the final amino acid). Consequently, every unbranched polypeptide chain possesses exactly two ends.

Final Conclusion
The primary structure of a protein molecule has two ends.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q14 - Non enzyme mediated reaction in biological system

questiontext.text: Enzymes are biocatalysts. They catalyse biochemical reactions. In general they reduce activation energy of reactions. Many physico-chemical processes are enzyme mediated. Which of the following reactions is not enzyme-mediated in biological system?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Enzymes are biological catalysts that increase the rate of chemical and biochemical transformations by lowering activation energy. While complex biochemical reactions and mechanical unwinding processes require enzyme catalysis, simple physical dissolution of gases in liquid occurs passively according to physical solubility laws.

Evaluation
Untwining DNA strands is an active process mediated by DNA helicases and topoisomerases; hydrolysis of sucrose into glucose and fructose is catalyzed by sucrase (invertase); and peptide bond synthesis is catalyzed by peptidyl transferase within the ribosome. In contrast, the physical dissolution of gaseous \(\text{CO}_2\) in water is a passive process that occurs spontaneously without an enzyme (although the subsequent chemical hydration of dissolved \(\text{CO}_2\) into carbonic acid is accelerated by carbonic anhydrase).

Final Conclusion
Dissolving \(\text{CO}_2\) in water is not an enzyme-mediated reaction in biological systems.
